content.user_title: Implement Code Step by Step from a Plan
content.value_statement: Large coding plans often fail when an agent edits too much at once. This skill implements one approved plan step at a time, keeps edits scoped, and reports a clear status when the step is done.
actual_capabilities: Implements one approved plan step at a time and keeps edits inside the agreed files.
Follows a fixed checklist that gates every code change on an explicit approval signal.
Routes work to isolated sub-windows and picks a cost-appropriate model tier per task.
Produces short status reports that start with DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS_CONTEXT.
Writes self-check notes for the Express lane and dispatch notes for the review role.
Records evidence, exit codes, and repair rounds for each implementation step.
limitations: Requires a prior plan step or approval marker before it will change any code.
The skill and its reports are written in Chinese only.
Depends on surrounding reference files for detailed rules, so it is not standalone.
Does not perform code review itself and hands review to a separate role.

use_cases.title: Work Through a Personal Coding Plan
use_cases.description: Turn an approved plan into working code one step at a time and get a clear status after each step.

use_cases.title: Add a Developer Role to an Agent Pipeline
use_cases.description: Slot a disciplined implementation stage into a multi-agent workflow that already has planning and review stages.

use_cases.title: Standardize Automated Code Changes
use_cases.description: Apply the same approval gates, scoping rules, and status format to every automated code change.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Single Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement Step 3 from the approved plan. Only edit the files listed in that step and report your status.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a written plan and want one step coded.

prompt_templates.title: Invoke the Developer Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as the developer role and implement Step 2 from the plan. End your reply with a status line.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want the developer role to pick up the next plan step.

prompt_templates.title: Implement and Self-Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement Step 5 from the plan. Run the step self-check and include the command and result for each verified item.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want the step coded and verified before review.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a Failed Attempt
prompt_templates.prompt: The last attempt at Step 4 failed. Write the root cause in one sentence, then open a new higher-tier repair round and report the outcome.
prompt_templates.scenario: A step keeps failing and needs a controlled repair round.

output_examples.input: Act as the developer role and implement Step 2 from the plan.
output: Changed: order service and its unit test
Self-check note written for the Express lane

output_examples.input: Implement Step 4, but the tests fail after your change.
output: Root cause: empty cart returns an undefined price
Repair round: 0 to 1, next round opens at a higher model tier
Needs: a decision from the planning role before more edits

output_examples.input: Implement Step 6 and confirm the tests pass.
output: Command run: test suite, result 42 passed, 1 skipped
Concern: one test path needs a real device and was not run

best_practices: Confirm an approval marker exists before editing any code.
Keep every change inside the files listed in the current step.
Attach a real command and exit code whenever you claim a task is done.
anti_patterns: Editing several plan steps in a single pass.
Changing code before the approval gate has passed.
Claiming a task is validated without a command and exit code.

faq.question: Does this skill write code without a plan?
faq.answer: No. It waits for an approved plan step or a recovery signal before it changes any file.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It works with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What does the skill output?
faq.answer: A short status report that starts with one of four states: DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, BLOCKED, or NEEDS_CONTEXT.

faq.question: Can it review code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It hands review to a separate review role and only prepares the dispatch notes.

faq.question: What language are the skill and its reports in?
faq.answer: The skill and the reports it writes are in Chinese.

faq.question: Does it work on its own?
faq.answer: It needs its reference and template files. The skill routes to those files for the detailed rules.
